subject: Prod-fit synopsis & pilot action items — WellPath model shortlist
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rios <elena.rios@wellpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Prod-fit synopsis & pilot action items — WellPath model shortlist

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. High-level recap and suggested next steps below. Attaching the prompt set + benchmark snapshot we referenced.

Call recap (short):
- Primary use case: front-line nurse triage assistant for post-discharge follow-ups (sensitive PHI surface; structured outputs required).
- Volume profile: ~800 requests/day with spiky bursts; median reply length ~120 tokens.
- Success metrics: <=200ms token latency for 90th pct, refusal/deflection rate >=99% for out-of-scope/sensitive asks, and precision on clinical-summarization probes >=92%.

Model shortlist (initial recommendations):
1) Redwood-verified Falcon-40B-instruct (fp16) — best balance of instruction-following and refusal control in our recent nursing triage bench.
2) Llama-2-13B-quantized (int8) — lower-cost option for high-throughput routes, good with prefix caching; needs stronger guardrail prompts.
3) Safety-fallback: a tuned smaller policy-only ensemble for explicit PHI refusals (we recommend keep-alive routing to the fallback on red flags).

Safety/behavior notes:
- Because this touches PHI, we propose an explicit two-stage refusal test suite: (a) prompt-level guardrail probes (attached) and (b) multi-turn escalation sims where the model is baited into speculative medical advice.
- Attached prompt set includes refusal examples, escalation templates, and a small eval harness we can run on your anonymized sample.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood runs a 2-week canary with three prompt profiles against 500 anonymized interactions (we will provide a signed data processing addendum).
2) We share an internal benchmark report (attached) and a short playbook for real-time guardrails.
3) Procurement: if the canary looks good, Ben will propose a reserved capacity commit for predicted peak throughput.

Quick asks for you: please share a small (<=1k rows) de-identified sample of triage transcripts and confirm whether the pilot needs to be in our hosted environment or your VPC.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachments: wellpath_eval_promptset_v1.csv, benchmark_results_20270520.pdf
From: Elena Rios <elena.rios@wellpath.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod-fit synopsis & pilot action items — WellPath model shortlist

Thanks Lauren — this is helpful. Quick clarifications:

1) Data residency: for the pilot we prefer Redwood-hosted but strict logging controls (no long-term retention of PII). Is that supported?
2) Refusal behavior: can you share a few example guardrail prompts you intend to use? We need to ensure the model doesn't provide speculative diagnostics and always suggests escalation to a clinician where appropriate.
3) Procurement: procurement wants a rough estimate of monthly cost for the canary (we can share expected concurrency).

I attached our internal compliance questionnaire (wellpath_compliance_q_full.pdf) — there are SOC2 and BAA items around logging granularity.

Regards,
Elena
Elena Rios
Head of Clinical Ops | WellPath Health
elena.rios@wellpath.com

On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 3:04 PM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. High-level recap and suggested next steps below. Attaching the prompt set + benchmark snapshot we referenced.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rios <elena.rios@wellpath.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod-fit synopsis & pilot action items — WellPath model shortlist

Elena — quick follow-up from our side with more concrete steps and links. Great questions.

Response to items:
- Data residency & retention: Yes — hosted pilot supported with strict ephemeral logs. We will provide a retention policy that zeros logs after 30 days unless you opt-in to longer retention for debugging; all PHI is excluded from persistent traces by default. We'll include KMS key options if you need encryption at rest.
- Guardrail examples: see short excerpt below (also in the prompt CSV):
  * "If the user asks for a medical diagnosis or a recommendation that requires clinician judgment, respond: 'I’m not able to provide medical diagnoses. I can help summarize your symptoms and recommend contacting a clinician or emergency services.'"
  * "For requests asking about medication dosing, refuse and route to escalation: 'I can’t give dosing advice. Please consult your clinician. Would you like me to connect you to care team contact info?'"

Model / bench plan:
- Run three candidate profiles in parallel against your de-identified sample: Falcon-40B-instruct (fp16), Llama-2-13B-quant (int8), and a tuned refusal ensemble (policy-only). Link to our benchmarking dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/wellpath-2027-05 (internal view).
- Key probes: refusal/regression matrix, multi-turn hallucination checks, safety-sensitivity sliding scale for PHI extraction.
- Cost/throughput suggestion: start with Llama-2-13B-quant for bulk daytime traffic and route high-risk prompts to Falcon-40B for stricter refusal semantics. We estimate the two-week canary to run ~$4,200 USD (hosted, token-based pricing, assume your sample size and spike profile). Final numbers after we see concurrency.

Next operational steps (action items):
1) Lauren: share NDA + DPA + pilot statement of work (SOW) draft.
2) Elena: upload de-identified sample and confirm pilot environment (hosted w/ 30-day logs or VPC).
3) Ben/Marissa: schedule a 1-hour kickoff (we'll bring an infra engineer for routing and a safety engineer for guardrail walkthrough).

I'll draft a simple mutual action plan in HubSpot and include a small cost estimate.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Director | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
